subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Which public opt-out contract should OpenClaw support for built-in skill sources such as `agents-skills-personal`?
rationale: The code evidence supports the problem, but adding a `skills.load` setting changes public config semantics and built-in source behavior, which repository policy reserves for maintainer product/API judgment.

options.title: Typed disabled source list
options.body: Add a default-empty `skills.load.disabledSources` style list over known source IDs and apply it consistently to discovery, watching, status, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow personal-source toggle
options.body: Add only a personal `.agents/skills` toggle, minimizing surface area but leaving future source opt-outs as separate product decisions.

options.title: Keep current source scanning
options.body: Do not add a source-level opt-out and instead rely on per-skill disables or agent allowlists despite the reported bulk-management and token-cost limitations.

recommendation.title: Typed disabled source list
recommendation.body: Add a default-empty `skills.load.disabledSources` style list over known source IDs and apply it consistently to discovery, watching, status, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current loader, watcher, and config files blame to Peter Steinberger, making this the strongest current-main owner signal for deciding the config surface.
